correctness.rationale: For every finite dimension and fixed positive cap vector, feasibility is equivalent to b≤Σu_i(a_i)_+. Strict feasibility gives lower approximation of every base feasible point via interpolation with a strict-slack vertex, and compactness plus uniqueness give continuity. At equality the feasible set is exactly the maximizing face; outer semicontinuity places all optimizer limits there. For every chosen point of that face, the written epsilon perturbation produces exactly that optimizer by the clipped Lagrangian certificate with multiplier 1/epsilon, proving complete attainment and sharp Euclidean jump. Exact rational check on the distributed verify.py passed 3512 assertions, including strictly feasible perturbations. The infinite proof is analytic and does not rely on enumeration.

originality.rationale: The main source, arXiv:2507.14488v2 §3.2 (Eq. 3.9, pp. 9–11), defines the same unique Euclidean box/halfspace minimizer and claims continuity in input parameters, but does not classify singular feasible-input boundaries. At zero constraint coefficients on the feasible-margin boundary, this theorem constructs every point of the maximizing face as an exact KKT-certified limit and identifies the sharp discontinuity set and norm jump. Classical projection references cover the clipped-multiplier formula only, which is not claimed as new. The accessible 2006 solution-map paper considers only linear-part perturbations rather than moving the constraint normal. The closest indexed findings concerning capped-simplex limiters, degeneracy of other constraints, and parametric quadratic programs use different constraints and do not imply the present exact cluster set.
residual_risks: The full text of Lee–Tam–Yen (2006) was restricted; its abstract alone cannot definitively exclude a comparable general lemma.

Generic parametric optimization sensitivity theory may contain an abstract broader statement; the claimed originality is the explicit exact classification for this limiter, not first observation of loss of regularity.

value.rationale: The motivating 2025/2026 paper invokes the parameter continuity of its quadratic knapsack limiter to explain improved temporal regularity. The derived necessary-and-sufficient continuity locus, exact boundary cluster face and sharp cap-dependent jump identify a precise structural limitation and a strict-feasibility condition that avoids it. They enable meaningful robustness assumptions for numerical entropy limiting without claiming a PDE trajectory encounters the degeneracy. A full classification and sharp magnitude for a natural computational subproblem have mathematical value beyond a one-off counterexample.
